The '''Korteweg-de Vries Institute for Mathematics (KdVI)''' is the institute for mathematical research at the [[University of Amsterdam]]. The KdVI is located in [[Amsterdam]] at the [[Amsterdam Science Park]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Korteweg-de Vries Institute for Mathematics|url=https://www.narcis.nl/organisation/RecordID/ORG1235559/Language/en|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2021-01-11|website=NARCIS}}</ref>

[[Robbert Dijkgraaf]], [[Alexander Schrijver]], [[Nicolai Reshetikhin]], [[Jacob Korevaar]], [[Miranda Cheng]], [[Harry Buhrman]] and Jan van de Craats are notable researchers connected to the institute. The KdVI is an institutional member of the [[Royal Dutch Mathematical Society]]<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Instituutsleden|url=https://www.wiskgenoot.nl/index.php?page=21|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2021-01-11|website=www.wiskgenoot.nl|language=nl}}</ref> and the [[European Mathematical Society]].
<ref>{{Cite web|title=Korteweg-de Vries Institute for Mathematics, Universiteit van Amsterdam {{!}} European Mathematical Society|url=https://euro-math-soc.eu/corporate/korteweg-de-vries-institute-mathematics-universiteit-van-amsterdam|access-date=2021-01-11|website=euro-math-soc.eu|archive-date=2021-02-25|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210225084306/https://euro-math-soc.eu/corporate/korteweg-de-vries-institute-mathematics-universiteit-van-amsterdam|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Research==
Among the core research directions of the KdVI are:<ref>{{cite web |title=Research |url=https://kdvi.uva.nl/research/research.html |website=kdvi.uva.nl |access-date=18 December 2025 |language=English}}</ref><ref name=":0" />
*[[Algebraic geometry]], prof.dr. Lenny Taelman
*[[Representation theory]], [[Lie theory]] and [[algebraic group]]s, prof.dr. Jasper Stokman and prof.dr. [[Eric Opdam]]
*[[Theoretical physics]] and [[mathematical physics]], prof.dr. Sergey Shadrin
*[[Discrete mathematics]], [[algebraic combinatorics]] and [[graph theory]], prof.dr. [[Jo Ellis-Monaghan]]<ref>{{Cite web|last=Ellis-Monaghan|first=Jo|date=|title=Jo Ellis-Monaghan|url=https://sites.google.com/site/joellismonaghan/home-1|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2021-01-11|website=sites.google.com|language=en-US}}</ref>
* [[Quantum Information]], dr. Jeroen Zuiddam
*[[Analysis (math)|Pure analysis]] and [[dynamical system]]s, prof.dr. Han Peters 
*[[Numerical analysis]] and applied analysis, prof.dr. Rob Stevenson
*[[Statistics|Mathematical statistics]] and [[machine learning]], prof.dr. Joris Mooij
*[[Probability theory]] and [[queueing theory]], prof.dr. [[Michel Mandjes]]
*[[Operations Research]], prof.dr. Sindo Nunez Queija
*[[History of mathematics]], dr. Gerard Alberts
*[[Didactic method|Didactics]], dr. André Heck
The institute is involved in several interdisciplinary research collaborations, including The Amsterdam String Theory Group,<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=11 January 2021|title=String Theory|url=https://iop.uva.nl/content/research-groups/strings/index.html|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2021-01-11|website=Institute of Physics - University of Amsterdam|language=en}}</ref> the NETWORKS programme<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.thenetworkcenter.nl/ |title=Home |website=thenetworkcenter.nl}}</ref> and the QuSoft research center for quantum software<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.qusoft.org/ |title=Home |website=qusoft.org}}</ref>

==Education==
Besides its research activities, the KdVI runs the education programmes in mathematics at the University of Amsterdam, namely the bachelor programme ''Mathematics''<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Bachelor Wiskunde|url=https://www.uva.nl/programmas/bachelors/wiskunde/wiskunde.html|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2021-01-11|website=Universiteit van Amsterdam|language=nl}}</ref> and the master programmes ''Mathematics''<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Master's Mathematics|url=https://www.uva.nl/en/programmes/masters/mathematics/mathematics.html|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2021-01-11|website=University of Amsterdam|language=en}}</ref> and ''Stochastics and Financial Mathematics'',<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Master Stochastics and Financial Mathematics|url=https://www.uva.nl/en/programmes/masters/stochastics-and-financial-mathematics/stochastics-and-financial-mathematics.html|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2021-01-11|website=Universiteit van Amsterdam|language=en}}</ref> and jointly organises interdisciplinary double bachelor programmes ''Mathematics and Physics'' and ''Mathematics and Computer Science''.<ref name=":1" />

==Name==
The institute is named after the mathematicians [[Diederik Johannes Korteweg]] and [[Gustav de Vries]]. Korteweg was professor of mathematics at the University of Amsterdam from 1881 to 1918, and De Vries was Korteweg's student. Together they worked on the [[Korteweg–de Vries equation]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=2 September 2020|title=D.J. Korteweg and G. de Vries - Korteweg-de Vries Institute for Mathematics|url=https://kdvi.uva.nl/about/korteweg-and-de-vries/korteweg-and-de-vries.html|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2021-01-11|website=Korteweg de Vries Instituut - University of Amsterdam|language=en}}</ref>
